items.title: The projection formula for a proper morphism between quasi-compact regular schemes with affine diagonal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for f : X -> Y a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with both X and Y quasi-compact, regular, of affine diagonal and finite dimension, f is a local complete intersection morphism, and that if moreover the Gysin map exists for f and f is proper then f_*(alpha . f^!beta) = f_*alpha . beta in CH^*(Y) otimes Q for the intersection product of the regular section (statement lines 13912-13926). The first assertion is More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-morphism-regular-schemes-is-lci; the proof notes f^![Y] = [X] by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy, writes alpha = ch(alpha') cap [X] and beta = ch(beta') cap [Y] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect) otimes Q as in the construction of that intersection product, and sets c = ch(alpha'), c' = ch(beta') (proof lines 13928-13940). The conclusion is then a six term chain: replace beta by its description, move f^! past the bivariant class c' using Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, substitute f^![Y] = [X], reorder the two cappings using that Chern classes are central in the bivariant ring, commute c' with f_* by bivariance, and read the result back as beta . f_*alpha (proof lines 13942-13960). Recognising that the regularly embedded situation admits the same bivariant bookkeeping as the smooth case, with the Chern character providing the bridge to K-theory, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
